scope: Find why reduced playback Worker time does not reliably increase displayed model FPS, improve verified host-side bottlenecks, and preserve rendering results.

outcome.remainingCriterion: A stable real-FPS uplift under comparable GPU availability is not verified. Current FPS results are inconclusive and must not be reported as an FPS speedup.

environment.gpuAvailability: User explicitly reported substantial concurrent GPU work during these measurements. No other task was stopped or reconfigured. rAF itself varied materially; GPU pressure is a known confound, not proof that all residual costs are GPU-only.

fixes.cause: The previous smoothed end-to-end response duration was also a minimum interval for future simulation timestamps. A transient delayed response stretched later deadlines even after production recovered.
fixes.change: Predict from observed display cadence and catch up to elapsed wall time; remove the stale compute-duration floor. Use rAF timestamps for cadence so callback scheduling delays are not sampled as refresh intervals.
fixes.reproduction: After a simulated 100ms delayed response the old next requested timestamp was 200ms; the corrected expectation is 116.6667ms. Both a deterministic unit test and a real browser Worker integration test fail on the original source at this assertion.

fixes.cause: When the prediction queue was full, its next replacement request was sent only after synchronous frame application and drawing finished.
fixes.change: Refill predictions before the synchronous presentation callback. Pending input remains deferred until the newly presented checkpoint is available. Keep one in-flight request and the existing three-frame prediction limit.
fixes.reproduction: The first submission callback observed only three requests on the original source; the regression requires the fourth replacement request to have already started. A separate pending-input regression checks the submitted checkpoint identity.

fixes.cause: Every decoded frame created new part color/property objects even when all seven Float64 color/opacity values and the immutable template were unchanged. This defeated the existing identity cache in applyPartRenderProperties and repeated filter configuration.
fixes.change: Retain the latest exact numeric sample and immutable properties per template. Compare with Object.is, including signed zero. Changed values and replacement templates create new snapshots; queued frames keep their prior properties. No frame colors, geometry or shader arithmetic are approximated.
fixes.reproduction: The original decoder fails the unchanged-property identity regression. Template replacement, delayed readers, changing opacity, visibility/render flags and signed zero remain covered.
fixes.ownership: One latest sample per immutable template in the stream-owned WeakMap. No frame history or cross-player cache.

raw.method: Actual renderer applyPreparedFrame, 16 decoded static frames cycled; rendering, mask drawing and GPU submission omitted. Both source fixture builds resident; 160 warmup applications and six ABBA samples of 120 applications per variant. This is CPU-side geometry/property application, not FPS.

cpuApplicationExperiment.limitations: Fixture-only full-player builds expose the actual renderer applyPreparedFrame method. Six ABBA samples per variant, each 120 applications, after 160 warmup applications. Sixteen real decoded static model frames are cycled. Drawing and GPU submission are omitted. This measures host geometry/property application and is not total Worker time or real FPS.

resident.method: Both builds load once in one visible Chrome page. Only one player runs and is visible; the other is paused and its input flush completed. Three ABBA cycles, 2s warmup and 5s observation per segment. Both GPU contexts remain resident. This removes repeated model-loading work but still cannot remove concurrent GPU contention.
resident.interpretation: Medians and means do not establish a consistent uplift; do not quote the small median difference as an FPS gain.

fps.limitations: observedModelFPS counts model updates observed on browser animation frames, not physical panel scanout. All runs, including non-improving runs and reduced rAF rates, are retained. Different GPU availability and changing rAF ceilings prevent attributing raw FPS changes solely to these code changes.

diagnostics.method: Temporary source copies and Worker wrappers only; nested Date.now measurements have 1ms granularity and add overhead. Individual runs had different external GPU load. Main stage values and request/response traces locate work and waits, but their before/after wall times are not a controlled speedup measurement. Raw event streams stay in the evidence directory.

quality.limits: Controlled old/new SSAA/MSAA, document/input bursts, buffering changes, resize, renderer recreation and main/Worker reference states are compared. Presentation timestamps intentionally recover differently after delay; numerical deformation and shader results at the tested states remain equal.

memory.limits: GC heap/backing-storage growth and logical resources were checked. Driver VRAM/RSS and an hours-long physical soak were not measured.

validation.puppetBuild: passed and reproduced measured player hash
validation.wallaby: MCP unavailable; global CLI failed because its installed bin/cli.js entrypoint is missing. Repository Vitest runners used.
validation.fixtureCorrections: The browser gate was rewritten without Promise.withResolvers to match the project TypeScript library target. A named refresh callback type resolves the formatter/linter function-type spacing conflict. These changes do not alter runtime behavior.

review.behavior: Verified scheduling and property-identity causes were fixed; numerical results and resource ownership checks passed. No remaining P0/P1/P2 defect was identified in the changed scope.
review.refactoring: Reuse existing scheduling and renderer contracts. Keep numerical interpolation, shader arithmetic and GPU resolution unchanged.
review.namingAndStructure: Changed production modules remain below 600 lines. No new dependency, package script, timer or production diagnostic hook.
verificationGaps: A stable actual-FPS uplift remains unverified under current concurrent GPU work.
Other browsers and physical low-end hardware were not benchmarked.
review.p0p1: None found in the changed scope.
